transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Ortega (Redwood SE), Jonas Park (Redwood Support), Priya Patel (Arcadia Dir Infra), Tom Reynolds (Arcadia SRE), Sarah Kim (Arcadia Sec PM), Marco Li (Arcadia NetEng)

Summary:
Quick status readout for the private pilot (VPC/on-prem) focusing on resilience tests, routing fallbacks, and the proposed kernel rollback handover. Decision points: agree to 48h soak with canary routing enabled, Redwood to deliver security pack and rollback playbook, schedule dry-run in maintenance window.

Topics:
- Routing fallback behavior and incident traces
- Kernel upgrade vs rollback (quantization kernels causing P95 spikes)
- Egress and VPC peering throughput issues on certain subnets
- Telemetry gaps and logging for audit/compliance
- Next steps and owners

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: ok uh hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45 minute sync, walk through the resilience tests and the weird p95 spikes we saw after the kernel push, Luca do you want to start with the telemetry highlights?
[00:32] Luca: yeah, sure, thanks Maya. quick note: the telemetry we have in the private pilot, there is a strong correlation between the kernel 2.1.4 quant path and p95 tailing on longer sequences, mostly in the egress-heavy flows to the third-party DM endpoints. p50 is fine, p95 jumps up like 200-300 ms in those windows.
[01:05] Tom: yep that's what we saw in prod-ish but in our staging the burst was amplified when we enabled batch sizes above 8. also we noticed connection churn on the peered VPC when MTU mismatched, Marco logged that, there's a couple of drops.
[01:28] Marco: mm-hmm, i captured three traces, i put them in the shared folder (link in chat), one of them shows retransmits from the NAT gateway, not sure if it's the on-prem router or the peering side.
[01:45] Priya: just to clarify, our main concern is stability during high-concurrency spikes for the scheduling service — if the inference latency jumps at p95 we get downstream timeouts and job reruns which cost us. also we need the security evidence for our audit next month.
[02:12] Maya: yes totally - security + reliability are the two gating factors. on the security side we'll send the SOC2 pack and the architecture diagram that shows KMS and SSO flows. on the reliability side Luca, can you outline the rollback vs patch options again?
[02:35] Luca: sure. option A: patch the kernel path to adjust the quantized matmul heuristics — that'll require a rebuild and a staged release, risk is small but time to deploy is ~72 hours with validation. option B: rollback to kernel 2.0.9 which was stable for the pilot; that gives immediate mitigation but we lose some perf optimizations and the newer kv-cache memory layout. option C: tune batching/cold-start caches on the request path to avoid the pathological sequence lengths we saw.
[03:07] Sarah: are there any data/disk schema changes tied to 2.1.4? we need to ensure rollback won't break audit logs or KMS-wrapped keys.
[03:18] Luca: no schema changes, it's purely execution kernels. KMS flows are unchanged. but there is a kv-cache binary layout difference if you persist checkpoints — we aren't persisting across the pilot, so rollback safe, but i'll document the caveat.
[03:39] Tom: the p95 spikes coincided with a bucket of long-context requests from our QA harness at 03:15 UTC, i can share the trace ids. also numa placement on the on-prem boxes appears to heat up causing context switch thrash, wonder if the new kernels are touching different CPU paths.
[04:06] Jonas: FYI we saw increased context switch rates in the system metrics, and on one host OOMs were avoided only due to the eviction policy kicking in, so memory churn is real.
[04:28] Maya: okay so immediate mitigation plan from Redwood is to offer rollback playbook and a canary routing toggle so Arcadia can send a percentage of traffic to the stable kernel while the rest stays on current. Luca, can you own the rollback playbook?
[04:46] Luca: yes i'll own that, i'll include pre-flight checks, step-by-step commands, and an automated validation script. also i'll include instructions for toggling canary routing in the control plane and how to pin model variants.
[05:10] Priya: when you say canary routing toggle, is that something non-disruptive? we don't want sessions to be dropped.
[05:22] Luca: it is non-disruptive for new requests; long-running streaming sessions will not automatically migrate mid-stream — we'll document session handling and fallback policies.
[05:37] Maya: good note. now networking: Marco, you mentioned MTU mismatches — what's the workaround?
[05:45] Marco: short term we can force PMTU discovery and set jumbo MTU on the on-prem switches to match cloud peering; medium term we'd like to add an egress shaping policy to reduce packet fragmentation.
[06:05] Tom: can we also run a focused throughput test on that subnet? i'll run a 2-hour stress test with the pilot config.
[06:15] Marco: yes i'll coordinate and we'll put the test traces into the shared folder.
[06:23] Sarah: on compliance — we need to ensure audit logs include token-level traceback for inference requests for certain endpoints. is that in the pilot telemetry?
[06:33] Jonas: we have token-level cost breakdown for hosted flows; for the private pilot we've been shipping similar traces but need to enable higher retention and the per-request audit log; that's an ops toggle we'll enable for Arcadia.
[06:50] Priya: good. also, SSO SAML: we want to validate role-mapping so that our teams get RBAC appropriate access to the telemetry console.
[06:59] Maya: Redwood will share the SSO doc; the mapping is standard but we'll include a sample SAML config and recommended groups.
[07:10] Tom: any blockers from Redwood side for the dry-run?
[07:15] Maya: primarily we need green light on maintenance window and acceptance of the rollback playbook; also we need Arcadia to run the 48h soak with canary routing enabled so we can observe behavior before full rollback.
[07:30] Priya: we can do the 48h soak, target starting 2027-11-20 00:00 UTC. we'll confirm but that aligns with our QA calendar.
[07:40] Luca: great. on telemetry gaps, i noticed some missing stack traces for the kernel oops events — we're going to push an updated exception-capture shim that collects more detailed symbols, but it requires a small agent restart. low risk but we should schedule.
[08:02] Sarah: please list that as a planned restart, we'll only approve outside business hours.
[08:10] Maya: noted. next, fallback policy behavior — quick demo: if a node falls below the latency SLO, requests should route to alternative pool, and if that pool is exhausted Redwood will return a 503 fallback with the configured degrade policy.
[08:30] Luca: i'll demo in the follow-up session, but the policy is configurable: percent routing, p95 threshold, and max failover concurrency. we also have a circuit-breaker so we don't over-surge the fallback.
[08:48] Tom: does the circuit-breaker maintain state across restarts? on our side restarts are frequent during upgrades so we don't want breaker to reset and flood the fallback.
[08:58] Luca: breaker state is persisted to local disk by default; there's an option to persist to a central store (Redis) which Arcadia can host for cross-host durability.
[09:12] Maya: ok that would help. Marco, can you spin up a small Redis instance in the VPC for stateful persistence during the soak?
[09:20] Marco: yes i can provision one, will follow least privilege and TLS.
[09:26] Priya: security question: KMS integrations — does Redwood support our HSM-backed keys?
[09:32] Maya: we integrate with standard KMS providers and can support external HSM via customer-managed KMS; we'll include the integration notes in the pack.
[09:44] Sarah: also need to know retention windows for audit logs and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM (we use Splunk).
[09:52] Jonas: logs can be exported via streaming to Splunk or S3; retention is configurable per-customer, we'll propose a default and docs.
[10:04] Priya: ok good. any open concerns on capacity? we previously saw a sustained 80% GPU utilization with the 2.1.4 kernel, do we want to dial down batch sizes during the soak?
[10:18] Luca: yeah for the soak we recommend keeping batch size at 4 and max concurrency at the pilot baseline; we'll provide a config file to enforce those limits at the proxy.
[10:30] Tom: one operational ask — can Redwood provide a short list of model variants with expected latencies so we can map SLAs to critical endpoints?
[10:40] Maya: yes — we'll share a model performance matrix including p50/p95 under the pilot config and sequence length buckets.
[10:50] Priya: about the dry-run rollback, what rollback telemetry should we capture to assert success?
[10:57] Luca: capture p50/p95, CPU, mem, context switch rates, retransmit counts, and a sample of failing requests before and after. we'll provide a script that pushes a golden load and records these metrics.
[11:15] Tom: ok i'll run the golden load during the dry-run window.
[11:20] Maya: let's recap decisions: 1) Arcadia runs 48h soak with canary routing starting ~2027-11-20; 2) Redwood to deliver SOC2 + SSO/KMS docs and kernel rollback playbook; 3) schedule dry-run rollback in maintenance window (proposed 2027-11-24 02:00-04:00 UTC) pending approvals; 4) Arcadia to provide traces and p95 slices.
[11:50] Priya: agree, i'll confirm maint window and people.
[12:00] Sarah: please also include the SIEM export instructions.
[12:07] Maya: yes, will include.
[12:14] Maya: any final questions?
[12:18] Tom: nothing from me, thanks.
[12:21] Marco: no questions.
[12:24] Luca: i'll start the playbook draft after this and share a link.
[12:29] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the action items.

End of transcript.
